rules.concept: Square palm with squared-off fingertips ('useful hand')
rules.explanation: In traditional palmistry a square palm with squared fingertips points to a practical, orderly temperament: someone who values routine, clear rules and dependable results, works steadily, and prefers methods that have already proved themselves. The same tradition says the downside can be reluctance to try unfamiliar ideas.

source.locator: Part I, ch. III 'The Square Hand and its Subdivisions' (chapter starts p. 28)

rules.concept: Square hand with short square fingers
rules.explanation: Read as a down-to-earth, results-minded nature that likes tangible proof and builds security gradually. The tradition adds that it can come with stubbornness and a narrow field of interest.

source.locator: Part I, ch. III 'The Square Hand and its Subdivisions' (chapter starts p. 28)

rules.concept: Square hand with long square fingers
rules.explanation: Read as a more analytical version of the square hand: careful, methodical reasoning that tests things before accepting them. Traditionally linked with work that rewards logic and systematic study.

rules.concept: Square palm with very long, pointed fingers
rules.explanation: Read as a person of good intentions whose plans can be pulled around by mood, so projects are started with enthusiasm but not always finished. A traditional pattern, not a fixed trait.

rules.concept: Spatulate hand: fingertips flared like a small spade
rules.explanation: Traditionally read as an energetic, restless and independent temperament that likes action, exploring and doing things its own way. People with it are associated with originality and a willingness to break from convention. A softer, flabbier version is read as the same restlessness with more irritability.

rules.concept: Philosophic ('knotty') hand: long, bony, with prominent finger joints
rules.explanation: Traditionally read as a reflective, analytical and private temperament: someone who looks for understanding more than material reward, thinks things through, and tends to keep their own counsel. The tradition also notes a proud, self-contained streak.

rules.concept: Conic hand: medium size, tapering palm, full-based fingers with rounded tips
rules.explanation: Read as a warm, impulsive and sociable temperament that responds quickly to beauty, music and other people's feelings. Quick to grasp ideas and good company, but traditionally described as less patient with long, repetitive effort.
